questions.text: Describe your experience with genomic data analysis pipelines. How have you handled raw sequencing data, quality control, and variant calling?

key_points: Data preprocessing steps (FASTQ cleaning, adapter trimming)
Quality assessment with FastQC or similar tools
Variant calling with GATK or FreeBayes
Annotation and filtering of variant calls
strong_answer_signals: Hands-on experience with tools like FastQC, Trimmomatic
Understanding of quality metrics and thresholds
Reproducible pipeline design with documentation
avoid: Theoretical knowledge only with no tool examples
Listing tools without explaining workflow logic

questions.text: Walk me through how you would approach a BLAST analysis for identifying homologous genes. What parameters would you optimize and why?

key_points: Database selection (nr, nt, protein vs nucleotide)
Multiple query handling and batch processing
strong_answer_signals: Knowledge of e-value thresholds, word size impacts
Understanding of compositional biases and low-complexity filtering
Ability to troubleshoot and validate BLAST results
avoid: Generic BLAST usage without optimization reasoning

questions.text: Tell me about a time you implemented a multiple sequence alignment project. What challenges did you face and how did you overcome them?

key_points: Tool selection based on dataset size and sequence types
Handling of divergent sequences and gap penalties
strong_answer_signals: Specific alignment strategies based on sequence similarity
Methods for handling gaps and indels appropriately
Clear explanation of tool selection rationale
avoid: Tool names only without implementation details

questions.text: Explain your experience with phylogenetic tree construction. How do you ensure the reliability of your phylogenetic inferences?

key_points: Model selection for sequence evolution (GTR, HKY85)
Tree building method choice (NJ, ML, Bayesian)
strong_answer_signals: Bootstrapping methods and convergence diagnostics
Model selection criteria (AIC, BIC)
Understanding of molecular clock assumptions
avoid: Superficial understanding of tree building algorithms
Skipping model selection and support assessment

questions.text: Describe a situation where you predicted protein structure. What methods did you use and how did you validate the results?

key_points: Homology modeling vs. ab initio prediction approaches
strong_answer_signals: Validation with RMSD calculations against crystal structures
Community servers usage (SWISS-MODEL, Phyre2, AlphaFold)
Understanding of model confidence scores

questions.text: Share an example of building a bioinformatics pipeline. How did you handle scalability and reproducibility?

strong_answer_signals: Pipeline automation with defined input-output relationships
Workflow management tools implementation
Clear documentation for pipeline reproduction
avoid: Manual workflow steps or inconsistent environments

questions.text: How do you stay current with bioinformatics tools and methodologies? Give me a specific example of a new tool you implemented.

key_points: Journal reading, conference attendance, online communities
Evaluating tool merit on benchmarks and documentation
Knowledge sharing within team or organization
strong_answer_signals: Specific tool integration with measurable impact
Comparison of new vs. old approach effectiveness
Evidence of continuous learning habits

questions.text: Walk through your experience with RNA-seq analysis. How do you handle differential expression analysis and batch effects?

key_points: Read alignment to reference genome (STAR, HISAT2)
Batch effect identification and correction strategies
strong_answer_signals: DESeq2 and edgeR usage with proper normalization
Batch correction with ComBat or SVA methods
Validation with independent datasets or qPCR
avoid: Just counting reads without proper normalization
Ignoring batch effects in experimental design
Differential expression without multiple testing correction

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked with CRISPR technology. What was your role and what were the key outcomes?

key_points: Guide RNA design and off-target prediction tools
Data analysis from CRISPR screens or editing experiments
Interpretation of gene function from results
strong_answer_signals: Specific targets identified and validated experimentally
Methods for detecting off-target effects or editing efficiency
Clear outcome measurement and biological interpretation
avoid: Only theoretical CRISPR knowledge or design considerations
Guide RNA design without validation steps

questions.text: Explain how you would design a GWAS study. What statistical considerations and quality controls are essential?

key_points: Sample size calculation and power analysis
Quality control for genotypes and phenotypes
strong_answer_signals: Power analysis and effect size considerations
Population structure control (PCA, kinship matrices)
Replication strategy and result validation
avoid: Using no multiple testing correction thresholds
Design without replication or validation plan

questions.text: Describe your experience with systems biology modeling. How do you integrate different data types?

key_points: Integration of omics data (transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics)
strong_answer_signals: Data integration strategies using common identifiers
Model validation with cross-validation or holdout sets
Ability to interpret biological insights from models
avoid: Just connecting data types without integration strategy

questions.text: Share an example of biomarker discovery work you've been involved in. What was your contribution and the impact?

key_points: Statistical validation methods (ROC curves, AUC values)
Biomarker panels vs. single marker approaches
strong_answer_signals: Biomarker validation with appropriate statistical methods
Clear articulation of clinical or research impact
Understanding of statistical power for biomarker detection
avoid: Just naming biomarkers without validation evidence

questions.text: How do you approach drug discovery bioinformatics tasks? Give me specific examples of your work.

strong_answer_signals: Target identification with pathway and network analysis
Hit-to-lead optimization with SAR analysis
Integration of multiple prediction models

questions.text: Tell me about your experience with structural bioinformatics. How do you analyze protein-ligand interactions?

key_points: Docking algorithms and scoring functions (AutoDock, Vina)
strong_answer_signals: Scoring functions understanding and calibration
Binding mode validation with experimental data
Interpretation of interaction energetics
avoid: Only structural theory without computational methods

questions.text: Describe how you've handled population genetics analysis. What specific challenges did you face?

key_points: Fst and other population differentiation metrics
strong_answer_signals: Population structure detection with appropriate methods
Migration or demographic pattern interpretation
Awareness of sampling bias and limitations

questions.text: Explain your experience with epigenetics data analysis. How do you handle different modification types?

strong_answer_signals: Integration with expression data for regulatory inference
Peak quality assessment and artifact removal
Differential analysis with proper controls
avoid: Only methylation analysis ignoring other marks

questions.text: Share an example of biostatistics work in biology. How did you handle complex statistical models?

key_points: Mixed effects models for hierarchical data
strong_answer_signals: Model validation with diagnostic plots and residuals
Interpretation of model coefficients biologically
Assessment of model assumptions and limitations

questions.text: How do you approach machine learning in biological applications? Give me a specific project example.

key_points: Feature engineering for biological data types
Model interpretation and biological insight extraction
Validation with independent test sets or experiments
strong_answer_signals: Model interpretation methods (SHAP, LIME, feature importance)
Biological insights derived from model predictions
Validation beyond metrics (experimental follow-up)
avoid: Generic ML descriptions without biological context
Black box models without interpretability focus

questions.text: Describe your experience with NCBI/Ensembl databases. How have you used them in your work?

key_points: API usage (Entrez Programming Utilities, REST APIs)
strong_answer_signals: API usage for programmatic data retrieval
Data retrieval efficiency and error handling
Annotation parsing and data integration
avoid: Only manual database searching through web interfaces
Ignoring API rate limits and query optimization

questions.text: Tell me about a bioinformatics pipeline you've optimized. What bottlenecks did you identify and how did you resolve them?

strong_answer_signals: Speed improvements with quantifiable metrics
Resource optimization (CPU, memory, storage)
Systematic bottleneck identification approach
